## Manuscript contract
- Title: **Protocol-Induced Uncertainty Limits AI Screening of Piezoelectric Materials**

### Research questions
- How large is cross-protocol disagreement for complete piezoelectric tensors after strict structure and convention alignment?
- Is disagreement mechanistically amplified by soft optical modes and large ionic-response sensitivity?
- Can a symmetry-equivariant probabilistic model predict both source-conditional tensors and their protocol disagreement with calibrated uncertainty?
- How does protocol uncertainty alter model leaderboards and the ranking of candidate materials?

### Planned contributions
- \textbf{\CrossPiezo benchmark.} A versioned, provenance-preserving benchmark of matched and unmatched MP and JARVIS piezoelectric records, with exact tensor convention conversion, structural match tiers, and frozen source/version/OOD splits.
- \textbf{Mechanistic protocol sensitivity.} A first-order perturbation analysis of the ionic piezoelectric response and a mode-resolved sensitivity score tested against observed cross-protocol discrepancies.
- \textbf{\PULSE model.} A source-conditional equivariant distributional model in symmetry-adapted tensor coordinates, separating a computational center from protocol contrast without claiming an unobservable ``true'' tensor.
- \textbf{Symmetry-compatible calibration and robust screening.} Source-stratified calibrated tensor regions and lower-confidence-bound screening of coupled electromechanical metrics.
- \textbf{Leaderboard stress test.} A comparison of modern tensor models under conventional in-source splits, cross-source counterfactual tests, database-version shifts, chemistry/prototype OOD, and high-sensitivity strata.

### Preregistered hypotheses
- H1: Uncertainty floor: Cross-protocol tensor disagreement is not negligible relative to in-source SOTA model error.
- H2: Mechanistic amplification: Disagreement increases with soft-mode sensitivity and ionic-response fraction after controlling for chemistry and structure mismatch.
- H3: Leaderboard fragility: Architecture rankings under random in-source splits differ from rankings under source-held-out and paired-counterfactual tests.
- H4: Calibration value: Source-conditional calibration improves coverage and risk--coverage behavior without excessive loss of sharpness.
- H5: Decision value: Robust screening yields higher cross-protocol or adjudication-set hit rate than ranking by a single-source point estimate.

### No-Go / downgrade conditions
- fewer than \TBD{300--500} high-confidence paired tensors remain after strict matching;
- paired disagreement is small relative to model error across almost all strata;
- disagreement is dominated by recoverable convention errors rather than protocol effects;
- soft-mode sensitivity has no reproducible relationship with disagreement;
- source-aware modeling does not improve calibration or robust decision quality;
- the third-protocol set, if run, does not support the robust-ranking claims.
